successCriteria.description: The `BalanceStatus` enum is defined locally in `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with exactly three members: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED — each a string enum value matching its key.

The `LeaveBalance` interface exposes all canonical fields: `id`, `employeeId`, `leavePolicyId`, `totalEntitlement`, `usedDays`, `remainingDays`, `fiscalYear`, `status: BalanceStatus`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt` — with correct types (string for IDs, number for numeric fields, Date for timestamps).

`IBalanceRepository` declares all seven methods: `findById`, `findByEmployee`, `findByEmployeeAndPolicy`, `findByEmployeeAndFiscalYear`, `create`, `update`, `delete` — with correct signatures matching the phase spec.

`IBalanceService` declares all seven methods: `getById`, `getByEmployee`, `getByEmployeeAndPolicy`, `create`, `deductDays`, `restoreDays`, `hasSufficientBalance` — plus `CreateBalanceDto` with fields `employeeId`, `leavePolicyId`, `totalEntitlement`, `fiscalYear`.

`BalanceService.create` validates that `totalEntitlement` is a positive finite integer and `fiscalYear` is a positive integer; rejects invalid input by throwing a `ValidationError` with a descriptive message.
`BalanceService.create` initializes `usedDays` to 0, sets `remainingDays = totalEntitlement`, and sets `status` to ACTIVE on the newly created balance.

`BalanceService.deductDays` floors the `days` argument, validates the balance is ACTIVE (rejects CLOSED and EXHAUSTED), checks sufficiency, increments `usedDays`, recalculates `remainingDays = Math.floor(totalEntitlement - usedDays)`, and transitions status to EXHAUSTED when `remainingDays` reaches 0.

`BalanceService.restoreDays` floors the `days` argument, rejects restoration on a CLOSED balance, validates `usedDays >= days`, decrements `usedDays`, recalculates `remainingDays`, and transitions status back to ACTIVE when `remainingDays > 0`.

`BalanceService.hasSufficientBalance` returns `false` (never throws) when no balance exists for the given employee+policy pair, when the balance status is not ACTIVE, or when `remainingDays < requestedDays` (after flooring `requestedDays`). Returns `true` only when an ACTIVE balance exists with `remainingDays >= requestedDays`.

Jest unit tests in `tests/unit/modules/balance/` cover: deduction happy path, deduction with insufficient balance, deduction on EXHAUSTED balance, deduction on CLOSED balance, restoration happy path, restoration on CLOSED balance, restoration exceeding used days, sufficiency check (true/false/not-found/non-ACTIVE), status transitions (ACTIVE→EXHAUSTED on deduction to zero, EXHAUSTED→ACTIVE on restoration), and edge cases (fractional days, zero, negative, NaN, Infinity).

constraints: The balance module MUST NOT import from `src/modules/policy/` or `src/modules/employee/` at this phase. It is self-contained; `leavePolicyId` and `employeeId` are plain string references. Cross-module validation (e.g., verifying `leavePolicyId` references a real policy) is deferred to Phase 6 (leave module).

entityInvariants.invariant: `remainingDays` is always `Math.floor(totalEntitlement - usedDays)`. It is never set independently — every mutation (create, deduct, restore) recalculates it from the two source fields.

Status lifecycle: a new balance starts ACTIVE. When `remainingDays` reaches 0 (via deduction), status transitions to EXHAUSTED. When `remainingDays` becomes > 0 (via restoration), status transitions back to ACTIVE. CLOSED is a terminal state — once CLOSED, no deduction or restoration is permitted.
`usedDays` must never exceed `totalEntitlement`. `usedDays` must never go below 0. Both are enforced by the service methods (deductDays checks sufficiency; restoreDays checks `usedDays >= days`).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Throws ValidationError for: non-positive/finite days argument, balance not found, balance status is CLOSED, balance status is not ACTIVE (including EXHAUSTED), insufficient remainingDays. The `days` argument is floored before use.
